chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Near-misses joining the Ellington band
summary: Duke Ellington heard him at a jam session in Indianapolis and later asked him to join when Lawrence Brown was leaving, but Brown stayed.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, he was singing when he played.
You made a record with Johnny.
Oh, I made several records with Johnny.
I always felt that you might have been very good in the Ellington band. Was there ever anything about that...?

Sort of once. Maybe a couple of times. Well, before Lawrence joined the band, in Indianapolis, Johnny and...uh...Freddy Jenkins... I was playing in Indianapolis, and they came to Indianapolis. And at this time, I wasn't working, but I went to a jam session; you know, jams...a sit-in thing. And they brought Duke in to hear me. And I was juiced back, so I... [LAUGHS] So right after that, he got Lawrence Brown to ...(?)... The next time, I was in Boston, and he asked me about coming with the band, and I said, "Okay" -- you know, because Lawrence was leaving. But Lawrence decided to stay, so I didn't go again. So that was the last...

Well, the last time I heard Duke, I was playing at some park out here. And Duke said to me, "Say, man, when are you join my band and see the world?" I said, "I've already seen the world!" [LAUGHS] This was about three or four years ago. I was with The World's Greatest Jazz Band, and the Duke Ellington band was on the same bill.
Was that out in Long Island?
